title: Catherine Spears Carpenter 1818 Casey County sweet-mash and sour-mash recipes
summary: An 1818 sheet in the Carpenter Family Papers at the Kentucky Historical Society holds two handwritten whiskey recipes, one for sweet mash and one for sour mash. The papers belonged to Catherine Spears Carpenter's Casey County family, though the sheet names no author.
bodyMarkdown:
Catherine Spears was born in Rockingham County, Virginia, in 1760. She came to Kentucky with her first husband, John Frye, and about 1779 they settled at Carpenter's Station in present-day Casey County. Frye was killed at the Battle of Blue Licks in 1782.

In 1784 she married Adam Carpenter, one of the station's founders. After his death in 1806 she ran the family farm herself until she died in 1848.

The Carpenter Family Papers, donated to the Kentucky Historical Society in 1995, include a single handwritten sheet of distilling recipes. One side gives a "Receipt for Distilling Corn Meal Sweet Mash." The other gives a "Receipt for Distilling by a Sour Mash," which starts the mash with hot slop left over from an earlier run. A note in different ink dates the sheet May 18, 1818.

The sheet names no author. The recipes are often called Catherine Carpenter's, but the Society's archivists say it is unclear whether she wrote them, used them, or kept recipes that were shared in the family or community. Either way, they are among the earliest written sour-mash directions known from Kentucky.

Sources: [Kentucky Historical Society, The Sour Mash Whiskey Recipe of Catherine Carpenter](https://history.ky.gov/kentucky-ancestors/the-sour-mash-whiskey-recipe-of-catherine-carpenter); [Kentucky Historical Society, MSS 47 Carpenter Family Papers finding aid](https://www.kyhistory.com/digital/api/collection/LIB/id/1909/download)
